name: Lobiani
steps: Mix the flour and yeast. Add 300 ml lukewarm water, 8 g salt and 20 ml oil; knead for 8–10 minutes until the dough is smooth and supple. Cover in a lightly oiled bowl and leave in a warm place for about 75 minutes, until almost doubled.

Finely chop the onion and garlic. Heat 20 ml oil in a pan over medium heat; cook the onion for 10–12 minutes until deep golden, then the garlic for 1 minute. Stir in the ground coriander, blue fenugreek and pepper for 30 seconds. Do not let the spices burn.

Add the well-drained kidney beans and remaining 4 g salt. Mash most beans with a potato masher, leaving some partly whole. Add up to the remaining 40 ml water only if needed to make a spreadable, thick filling; no liquid should pool in the pan. Cook for 2 minutes and cool completely before filling the bread.

Heat the oven to 230°C with a heavy tray inside for 25 minutes. Divide risen dough into two equal balls and the cool bean filling into two equal portions. Flatten one ball into a 20-cm disc. Place filling in the centre, draw the dough edges up around it and pinch closed. Turn seam-side down and gently press to a 25-cm round, keeping the filling enclosed. Repeat with the second.

Make a small steam hole in the top of each bread and rest covered for 10 minutes. Bake each on the hot tray for 15–18 minutes until puffed and golden brown, with a fully baked underside. Brush the two hot breads with the remaining 5 ml oil and rest 3 minutes.

Cut each round into four wedges and serve two wedges per person. A slice should show a generous, even layer of seasoned kidney beans between soft bread layers, with no cheese or animal-derived ingredients.
tips: This is a vegetarian, eggless lobiani without the ham used in some regional versions. Draining and cooling the beans keeps the dough from tearing. If blue fenugreek is unavailable, use 1 g ordinary ground fenugreek plus 1 g extra ground coriander, but expect a slightly different aroma.
passiveTime: 75 minutes dough rising and 10 minutes shaped-bread resting
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
